model: Symbio 400-B/500 Fan Coil, Blower Coil and Unit Ventilator
equipment_type: Fan coil, blower coil and unit ventilator controller
applies_to: Trane fan coils, blower coils and unit ventilators controlled by a Symbio 400-B or Symbio 500 programmable controller.
summary: The Symbio 400-B/500 is Trane's programmable unit controller, BTL listed as a B-BC. For fan coil, blower coil and unit ventilator applications it exposes about 115 objects: local and BAS sensor values, occupancy, heat/cool mode and fan speed requests, valve, damper and heat outputs, setpoint limits and diagnostics. Symbio UI sets the protocol and chooses BAS or local per sensor and setpoint.
notes: The guide has no read/write column; access is inferred (BAS, Request, Setpoint, Enable and Reset objects as writable; inputs, outputs, Active, Status and Diagnostic objects as read-only).
Each point exists only on units with the matching option (the guide has a "when the point exists" column: economizer, hydronic, DX, electric heat, ECM fan, CO2 and so on).
BO 4 is printed twice: Chilled Water Valve Command Binary, or Compressor 1 Command, depending on the unit type; the first is listed.
BO 6 is printed twice: Heating Valve Command Binary, or Electric Heat Output 1, depending on the unit type; the first is listed.
BO 7 is printed twice: Reversing Valve Output, or Electric Heat Output 2, depending on the unit type; the first is listed.
MO 1 and MV 8 are both printed with the name Supply Fan Speed BAS; MV 8 carries Auto/Off/Low/Medium/High.
MV 2 Cooling Fan Speed Default appears only in the alphabetical table, marked do not use.
Units shown are imperial; System Units in Symbio UI switch BACnet units to SI. The guide also offers IP settings on IP-capable controllers but describes MS/TP addressing.

source.title: Integration Guide - Symbio 400-B/500 Programmable Controller for Fan Coil, Blower Coil and Unit Ventilator

integration.summary: Set the rotary address, then use Symbio UI (USB, http://198.80.18.1) BAS Control Selection to pick BAS or Local for each sensor and setpoint. Schedule with MV 6 Occupancy Request, write AV 27 Space Temperature Setpoint BAS, MV 4 Heat Cool Mode Request and MV 8 fan speed, and refresh any BAS sensor objects at least every 15 minutes.

minimum_points.name: Occupancy Request
minimum_points.why: Occupancy command from the BMS schedule

minimum_points.name: Space Temperature Active
minimum_points.why: Space temperature the unit controls to

integration.enable: The BAS controls the unit by writing values and putting points in or out of service. BAS Control Selection in Symbio UI chooses BAS or Local per sensor and setpoint. MV 9 Emergency Override BAS shuts the unit down for any value other than 1 = Normal.
integration.heartbeat: BAS-supplied sensor objects (Space Temperature BAS, Outdoor Air Temperature BAS, Space Humidity BAS, Entering Water Temperature BAS) must be rewritten at least every 15 minutes. If no write is seen in time the object goes to fault and the unit falls back to its own sensor; at power-up they start in fault until written.
integration.remote_sensors: Put the BAS sensor objects in service (they are out of service by default), then write AV 14 Space Temperature BAS, AV 1 Outdoor Air Temperature BAS, AV 2 Space Humidity BAS, AV 4 Entering Water Temperature BAS or AV 112 Space CO2 Concentration BAS. The matching Active objects (AV 59, AV 3, AV 6, AV 5, AV 113) show the value in use.
setup: Three rotary switches set the BACnet MAC address and Device ID; each controller on a link needs a unique value.
Symbio UI (USB only, http://198.80.18.1) sets protocol, IP, identification and system units; saving restarts the controller.
Tracer SC+ sets a software Device ID automatically during discovery; third-party systems must set it themselves.
System units (IP/SI) chosen in Symbio UI change the units sent over BACnet.
gotchas: BAS sensor objects are out of service by default; put them in service before writing.
BV 2 Reset Diagnostic Request clears all diagnostics except Filter Change Required; BV 12 resets the filter timer. Both self-clear.
BO 4, BO 6 and BO 7 change meaning with the unit type (hydronic vs DX/heat pump vs electric heat).
Only the points for the unit's options are present.
